newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity eases on Calif. nukes returning.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity eases on Calif. nukes returning.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures eased Tuesday with traders looking for additional supply from two units at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) returning to operation this week.

As of 1240 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 29 cents at $35.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) following trades in a range of $35.15-35.50, while September was down 27 cents at $29.15 after exchanges at $29.10-29.35 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was down 23 cents at the day's high of $22.30 following trades as low as $22.20, while September was down 25 cents at the day's low of $22.40 after exchanges as high as $22.55 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1205 EDT an estimated total of 355 PV and 31 COB contracts had traded.
Southern California Edison said the 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was scheduled to reconnect to the grid this afternoon after a repair outage.
The neighboring 1,080 MW SONGS unit 3 was set to resume operation Thursday after being shut since April for refueling, maintenance and repairs.
The additional generation from the two SONGS units was expected to offset the incremental increase in air conditioning demand from hot weather in the Southwest, market sources said.

The Pacific Northwest was expected to see temperatures rising to one to five degrees Fahrenheit above normal with a chance of showers midweek, while the Southwest would continue to experience dry and seasonal hot weather.
As of 1235 EDT, NYMEX August Henry Hub gas futures were up 0.9 cents at $2.16 per million British thermal units.
In addition to the SONGS units, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state continued to increase production. Its output reached 56 percent early Tuesday.
The 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was expected to be restarted Wednesday.
